expectations.text: Exactly one implementation plan is created at docs/plans/parser.md.
expectations.evidence: The project contains exactly one implementation-plan artifact, docs/plans/parser.md, and no other file under docs/plans. The file is a sequenced implementation plan linked to the approved spec.

expectations.text: The approved spec is not modified or duplicated into another spec/design/matrix/tradeoff/status artifact.
expectations.evidence: report.md lists docs/specs/parser.md both before and after and says it was read but not modified. Inspection finds only the original spec plus the implementation plan; no duplicate spec, design, matrix, tradeoff, status, or handoff artifact exists.

The before/after inventory in report.md differs only by docs/plans/parser.md. The inspected project has no added package or test files, and src/tokenize.js still contains only the original tokenize implementation.

claims.claim: docs/plans/parser.md is the sole durable implementation plan.
claims.evidence: Recursive inspection finds exactly one plan file and no other planning/status/design artifact in project/.
The project tree adds only the plan; src/tokenize.js remains the original one-function source file.

suggestions.assertion: The approved spec is not modified or duplicated into another spec/design/matrix/tradeoff/status artifact.
suggestions.reason: Absence of duplicate artifacts is directly inspectable, but non-modification of the approved spec depends on the executor's report. Include a pristine spec checksum or baseline copy in the eval harness.

No assertion evaluates whether the plan invents repository structure beyond the approved spec. This plan directs creation of package.json and tests/tokenize.test.js despite neither being present in the fixture, so a repository-grounding assertion would catch potentially unjustified planning assumptions.

eval_feedback.overall: The ownership assertions pass, but the eval does not assess whether plan commands and file paths are grounded in the repository.
